items.followUp: Explain how temperature affects enzyme activity.

rubric.why: Identifies the pH at which an enzyme works best.
rubric.description: Each enzyme has an optimum pH at which it has maximum activity.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that an enzyme has an optimum pH for maximum activity.

rubric.why: Explains how pH changes reduce enzyme activity.
rubric.description: A pH above or below the optimum can change the enzyme’s structure and active site, reducing activity; extreme pH may denature it.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing a structural or active-site change, or denaturation, that reduces activity.

modelAnswer: Each enzyme has an optimum pH at which it has maximum activity.
A pH above or below the optimum can change the enzyme’s structure and active site, so its activity decreases; extreme pH may denature it.

items.followUp: What is enzyme denaturation, and what happens to the enzyme’s active site?

rubric.why: Defines denaturation as a change in enzyme structure and identifies a possible cause.
rubric.description: Denaturation is a change in an enzyme’s structure, often caused by high temperature or extreme pH.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the structural change or a cause of denaturation.

rubric.why: States the effect of denaturation on enzyme function.
rubric.description: The changed active site prevents proper substrate binding, so the enzyme loses its activity.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that the active site changes or that the enzyme loses function.

modelAnswer: Denaturation is a change in an enzyme’s structure, often caused by high temperature or extreme pH.
The active site changes shape, so the substrate cannot bind properly and the enzyme loses its activity.

items.followUp: Where is pericardial fluid found, and how does it protect the heart?

rubric.why: States the lubricating function of pericardial fluid.
rubric.description: Pericardial fluid lubricates the surfaces around the heart and reduces friction.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that it lubricates or reduces friction.

rubric.why: Connects the fluid’s function to the heart’s movement.
rubric.description: By reducing friction, the fluid allows the heart to move smoothly as it beats.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that it allows smooth heart movement during beating.

modelAnswer: Pericardial fluid lies between the membranes surrounding the heart.
It lubricates the surfaces, reduces friction and allows the heart to beat smoothly.

items.followUp: Describe unicellular, colonial and multicellular organisms, giving one example of each.

rubric.why: Describes unicellular organization or gives a suitable example.
rubric.description: A unicellular organism consists of one cell that performs all life functions; Amoeba is an example.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the defining feature of unicellular organisms or a suitable example.

rubric.why: Describes colonial organization or gives a suitable example.
rubric.description: In colonial organisms, similar cells live together in a group or colony; Volvox is an example.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing colonial organization or giving a suitable example.

rubric.why: Identifies multicellular organization or gives a suitable example.
rubric.description: Multicellular organisms consist of many cells, often specialized for different functions; humans are an example.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the defining feature of multicellular organisms or a suitable example.

rubric.why: Explains how specialized cells are organized to perform different functions.
rubric.description: Specialized cells work together through division of labour and may form tissues and organs.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating division of labour or describing organization into tissues and organs.

modelAnswer: In unicellular organisms, a single cell performs all the functions needed for life; for example, Amoeba.
In colonial organisms, similar cells live together in a group or colony; Volvox is an example.
Multicellular organisms consist of many cells, often specialized for different functions; humans are an example.
Specialized cells work together through division of labour and may form tissues and organs.

items.followUp: Explain how humidity, wind and the number of stomata affect the rate of transpiration.

rubric.why: Explains the effects of light and temperature on transpiration.
rubric.description: Bright light usually opens stomata and increases transpiration; higher temperature increases evaporation and usually raises the rate.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for correctly explaining both light and temperature effects.

rubric.why: Explains how humidity affects water-vapour loss.
rubric.description: Low humidity increases transpiration, whereas high humidity reduces it.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly explaining the effect of humidity.

rubric.why: Explains how wind affects the air around the leaf.
rubric.description: Wind removes moist air around the leaf and usually increases transpiration.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly explaining the effect of wind.

rubric.why: Identifies a leaf feature or water-supply factor that affects transpiration.
rubric.description: Larger leaf area or more stomata generally increases transpiration; a thick waxy cuticle reduces it. Adequate soil water supports transpiration, while water shortage may cause stomata to close.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct leaf-structure or water-availability factor and its effect.

modelAnswer: Light: bright light usually opens stomata and increases transpiration; darkness generally lowers it.
Temperature: higher temperature increases evaporation from leaf surfaces and usually raises the rate of transpiration.
Humidity: low humidity increases transpiration, while high humidity reduces the difference in water-vapour concentration and lowers it.
Wind: moving air removes moist air around the leaf, usually increasing transpiration.
Soil water: adequate water supply supports transpiration; water shortage may cause stomata to close and reduce it.
Leaf features: larger leaf area and more stomata generally increase transpiration, while a thick waxy cuticle reduces water loss.
